samples: This program reads a list of user records from a JSON file (the path `data/users.json` is hard-coded in `main`), keeps only the active users aged 18 or older, and prints their e-mail addresses one per line, sorted by user name, followed by a count line. It validates data as it loads: ages must be non-negative and e-mails must look plausible, and the program fails with a file or JSON error if the file can't be read or doesn't match that shape. It only needs permission to read files and write to the console, so it is safe to run, but you would need to change the hard-coded path (or call the reusable function directly) to use it on other files.

This program reads a JSON file of user records (hardcoded as `data/users.json`), keeps the users who are active and at least 18, and prints their e-mail addresses one per line, ordered by user name, followed by a count of how many were found. It only needs permission to read files and write to the console, and it fails with a file or JSON error if the file is missing or malformed. Records with a negative age or an e-mail that doesn't look like a plausible address will also fail to load, so the whole file must be valid for it to produce any output.

This program reads a JSON file of user records (hardcoded as `data/users.json`), keeps the users who are active and at least 18, and prints their e-mail addresses one per line, sorted by user name, followed by a count line. It validates that each user's age is non-negative and each e-mail looks plausible, and it fails with a file or JSON error if the file can't be read or doesn't parse into that shape. It only needs permission to read files and write to the console, so it is safe to run, but the input path is fixed and it is meant as a small report script rather than a configurable tool.

This program reads a JSON file of user records (hardcoded as data/users.json), keeps the users who are active and at least 18, and prints their e-mail addresses one per line, sorted by user name, followed by a count of how many were found. It checks that each e-mail looks plausible and that ages are non-negative, and it reports a failure if the file can't be read or the JSON doesn't match the expected shape. It only needs read access to the filesystem plus console output, so it is safe to run, but the input path is fixed in the main function, so you would need to call the reusable function from your own code to use a different file.

This program reads a JSON file of user accounts (hardcoded as data/users.json), keeps the active users who are at least 18, and prints their e-mail addresses one per line, ordered by user name, followed by a count line. It validates each user's age and e-mail format as the file is parsed, and it needs only read access to the filesystem and the console. If the file is missing or the JSON is malformed or invalid, it fails with an error instead of printing a partial list.
